label_th: ดีใจสุดขีด

body_cues.head: tilted back
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: up / toward the sky or the partner
body_cues.arms: both raised above shoulders, symmetrical, pumping up-down
body_cues.tempo_quality: fast, rhythmic, re-starting (Laban: free flow, light, rising)

silhouette_check: Arms above the head form a clear V/Y shape; very readable.

readability.disambiguate_with: Arms go UP and OUT and the body rises/advances; fear arms come in or forward and the body retreats.

cultural_caveats: Large public jumping is fine for youth/sport contexts; an older Thai character in a formal scene would usually contain it (craft judgement, unverified).
ai_prompt_phrase: jumping with both arms raised high, head thrown back, bouncing with joy

evidence.note: Dael: joy 90% classified, symmetrical up-down repetitive arm action; Kleinsmith: head back, arms raised; Melzer: jumping, rhythmic, spreading, rising.

label_th: สุขใจเงียบ ๆ

body_cues.head: slightly up, eyes-closed feel
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: averted upward or to the side, not at anyone
body_cues.spine_torso: upright but relaxed, slight lean back
body_cues.arms: one arm moving, asymmetrical (e.g. one hand on a warm cup)

silhouette_check: Head tilted up and away reads only if the profile is clear - use 3/4 or side view.

readability.disambiguate_with: Head UP and chest open (sadness: head down, chest closed); add a warm prop (tea, sun, breeze).

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: R.emote 'tender' minus the sad brows; R.lean(P,t,dur,-3)
ai_prompt_phrase: eyes closed, face tilted up toward the sun, relaxed shoulders, holding a warm cup

evidence.note: Dael cluster 9: head tilted up and averted + asymmetrical arm action was fairly prototypical of pleasure (but used in only 40% of pleasure portrayals).

label_th: ขำ หัวเราะ

body_cues.head: straight, bobbing with laughter
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: toward the person who made the joke
body_cues.spine_torso: folds forward on big laughs, rocks back
body_cues.arms: touching self (belly, knee) or the other person's arm
body_cues.tempo_quality: discontinuous: bursts with short holds in between

silhouette_check: Forward fold with hand on belly reads well in side view.

confusable_with: grief_despair (sobbing: shaking shoulders + forward fold looks similar)
readability.disambiguate_with: Head oriented to the partner and open chest between bursts; context line or laugh SFX.

cultural_caveats: Touching a peer's arm is fine; touching an elder or monk is not (general Thai etiquette, unverified detail).
rig_hint: R.squash repeated + small R.nod; hand pose 'chest' low
ai_prompt_phrase: laughing hard, bending forward, one hand on belly, other hand touching friend's arm

evidence.note: Dael: amusement 70% classified; touching/manipulation and discontinuous movements with holds, head straight toward interlocutor.

label_th: ภูมิใจ ชนะ

body_cues.head: tilted back slightly, chin up
body_cues.arms: raised above head or out from the body
body_cues.tempo_quality: stroke-and-hold: a quick rise, then a held pose

silhouette_check: Arms-out V with chest forward is the strongest silhouette in the library.

readability.disambiguate_with: Fists and a HELD pose = triumph; frustration adds hands to head or a downward hit.

cultural_caveats: Big pride displays can read as boastful in Thai settings that value modesty (kreng jai) - use for sport/achievement, not for social one-upmanship (cultural inference, unverified).
ai_prompt_phrase: victory pose, arms raised in fists, chest out, chin up

evidence.note: Tracy & Matsumoto: head back, arms raised, fists, chest expanded after winning in sighted AND congenitally blind athletes; hands on hips not reliably shown.

label_th: ภูมิใจเงียบ ๆ
intent: pleased with own work, not showing off

body_cues.head: level or slightly up
body_cues.arms: one hand on the object or both arms loosely folded
body_cues.tempo_quality: slow settle into a still pose

silhouette_check: Needs the object in frame to read.

readability.disambiguate_with: Head slightly back (pride) vs forward/turned away (disgust); look at the object.

cultural_caveats: Modest version suits Thai social norms better than pride_triumph (craft judgement).
ai_prompt_phrase: standing back to admire finished work, small satisfied posture, arms loosely folded

evidence.note: Head-back pride cue from research; the small, object-directed version is craft.

label_th: โล่งใจ
intent: tension released after a threat passes

body_cues.head: drops then lifts
body_cues.arms: fall to the sides or hand to chest
body_cues.tempo_quality: one big slow exhale: stillness -> sink -> settle

silhouette_check: A shoulder drop is small - show it in MS/MCU, not wide.

confusable_with: sadness_low (Dael grouped sadness and relief together: arms resting)
readability.disambiguate_with: Sequence matters: show the tense state first, then the drop; add an exhale SFX and lift the head at the end.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: shoulders dropping with a long exhale, hand on chest, head lifting with a relieved smile

evidence.note: Dael: relief (50%) shared the 'arms resting' cluster with sadness - so relief needs temporal context; exhale/head lift are craft.

label_th: สนใจ อยากรู้

body_cues.head: tilted slightly to one side
body_cues.arms: one arm active (reaching, pointing), the other at the side
body_cues.hands: one hand reaching or at chin

silhouette_check: Forward lean is visible in side or 3/4 view only.

confusable_with: irritation_cold_anger (same Dael cluster: trunk forward + one-arm action)
readability.disambiguate_with: Open, rounded shape and a reach toward the object; irritation is angular with a closed hand and turns toward a person.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: leaning in with head tilted, reaching toward the object with curiosity

evidence.note: Dael cluster 1 (arms at side, trunk forward, one-arm asymmetric action) grouped 30% of interest AND irritation portrayals; head tilt is craft.

label_th: เศร้า

body_cues.head: dropped forward
body_cues.arms: hanging straight down, close to the body, or touching the upper body

silhouette_check: Rounded C-curve of the spine with arms down is highly readable even from far.

readability.disambiguate_with: Sadness = slow + passive + head down; despair adds hands to face/head; tiredness adds yawning/rubbing.

cultural_caveats: Cross-culturally the best-agreed body expression (Japanese/Sri Lankan/American observers, Kleinsmith survey); no Thai data.
ai_prompt_phrase: slumped shoulders, head hanging down, arms limp at the sides, slow heavy steps

evidence.note: Coulson: some sadness postures >90%; Kleinsmith: arms straight down close to body is the core; Melzer: passive weight, sinking, head dropping; Pollick: slow, smooth.

label_th: สิ้นหวัง โศก

body_cues.head: in hands or thrown back
body_cues.arms: hands to face or head, or hugging self
body_cues.weight: collapsing - may sink to knees or sit

silhouette_check: Kneeling with face in hands is a classic readable shape.

readability.disambiguate_with: Covered face + collapse to the floor; sound design (sobs) and context carry the rest.

cultural_caveats: When sitting on the floor, mind feet direction. Seated or lying: keep the soles pointed away from other characters, elders and any Buddha image (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: sinking to the knees, face buried in both hands, shoulders shaking

evidence.note: Dael: despair had an indistinct body pattern shared with anxiety, and sadness was confused with despair - so the recognisable 'face in hands' version is a craft convention.

label_th: อับอาย ละอาย
intent: feel exposed after failure or wrongdoing

body_cues.head: lowered
body_cues.arms: close to the body
body_cues.distance: moves away / turns the back partly

silhouette_check: Narrow chest + dropped shoulders reads in silhouette; head down alone does not.

readability.disambiguate_with: Add a cause in frame (broken object, onlookers); shame turns away from the onlookers.

cultural_caveats: Tracy & Matsumoto found shame display stronger in less individualistic cultures; showing it is not 'over-acting' for a Thai audience (inference).
ai_prompt_phrase: shoulders slumped, chest caved in, turning away from the others, head bowed

evidence.note: Tracy & Matsumoto: only shoulders slumped and chest narrowed increased after losing; head-down was coded but not significant in their photos.

label_th: เขิน อาย
intent: minor social slip, wants it to pass

body_cues.head: lowered and turned to the side
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: down-away, then a quick look back
body_cues.arms: one hand to the face, neck or back of head
body_cues.legs_feet: toes turned in, one foot rubbing the other

silhouette_check: Hand to the back of the head is a readable cartoon convention.

readability.disambiguate_with: Embarrassment keeps a half-smile and glances back; shame stays turned away.

cultural_caveats: Scratching your own head is fine; Never touch or pat another character's head, even a child's (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: embarrassed, rubbing the back of the neck, looking down and to the side

evidence.note: Embarrassment is among the body-expressed emotions reviewed by Witkower & Tracy (abstract only); the specific cues here are craft conventions.

label_th: โกรธจัด

body_cues.head: forward, slightly down
body_cues.arms: bent, tense; may stab forward or strike down

silhouette_check: Forward diagonal lean with angular elbows; angular shapes read as threat.

readability.disambiguate_with: Anger is aimed AT someone (direction + approach); frustration is aimed at nothing.

cultural_caveats: Pointing a finger at someone's face is very confrontational; pointing with the foot is a grave insult in Thai culture - avoid unless the story needs it (ThailandFoundation2024 on feet).
ai_prompt_phrase: storming forward, leaning in, fists clenched, sharp jerky movements

evidence.note: Dael: hot anger homogeneously expressed by frontal lean/movement (70% classified); Melzer: strong, sudden, advancing, direct; Pollick: fast, jerky; Coulson: some anger postures >90%; Aronoff (via Kleinsmith): angular = threat.

label_th: หงุดหงิด โกรธเงียบ

body_cues.head: still, slightly down
body_cues.arms: crossed, or one arm making a small sharp gesture
body_cues.tempo_quality: mostly still with small repetitive actions

silhouette_check: Crossed arms read; the 'cold' quality depends on stillness - check in motion.

readability.disambiguate_with: Add the irritant (noise, late friend) and a repetitive tap; head straight, not tilted.

cultural_caveats: Open displays of anger are often softened in Thai interaction; cold, smiling irritation may be the more 'Thai-real' version (unverified cultural observation).
rig_hint: R.pose 'hug' (arms crossed approximation) + small repeated mv on foreR
ai_prompt_phrase: arms crossed, tapping foot, tight shoulders, staring flatly

evidence.note: Dael: irritation only 30% classified and shared a cluster with interest; tapping/crossed arms are craft.

label_th: หัวเสีย ขัดใจ

body_cues.head: thrown back or dropped into hands
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: up at the sky or down at the problem
body_cues.arms: raised and extended laterally, then dropping
body_cues.hands: hands to head, or a downward slap on the thigh/table
body_cues.distance: turns away from the obstacle, then back

silhouette_check: Hands on top of the head is a readable shape.

confusable_with: pride_triumph (Kleinsmith: both had shoulders up/back and arms raised laterally)
readability.disambiguate_with: Hands to the head or a downward hit; triumph holds the arms up with fists.

cultural_caveats: Hands on own head are fine. Never touch or pat another character's head, even a child's (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: throwing hands up then grabbing own head in frustration

evidence.note: Kleinsmith (Wii non-acted postures): frustrated and triumphant both shoulders up/back, arms raised laterally - arousal separated better than valence.

label_th: กลัว ตกใจกลัว

body_cues.head: pulled back, may duck
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: toward the threat, ready to look away
body_cues.spine_torso: leaning back, contracted, may twist laterally
body_cues.arms: pulled in or raised in front as a shield
body_cues.hands: open, fingers spread, in front of the body

silhouette_check: Leaning back with hands up in front reads in side view.

confusable_with: joy_elated (Dael: panic fear confused with elated joy 30%)
readability.disambiguate_with: Fear moves BACK and CONDENSES; joy moves UP and SPREADS. Show the threat or the character's head orientation toward it.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: recoiling backward, hands raised in front, shoulders hunched, stepping away

evidence.note: Melzer: retreating, condensing, bound flow, backwards, enclosing; Dael: backward lean, upward gaze, lateral trunk lean, symmetrical arm action with knee movement.

label_th: กังวล

body_cues.head: slightly down, small movements
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: flicking between the worry and nowhere
body_cues.arms: close to body
body_cues.hands: self-touch: wringing hands, rubbing arm, touching neck

silhouette_check: Hand-wringing at chest height reads in MS.

readability.disambiguate_with: Repetitive self-touch + glances toward the source of worry (phone, door, letter).

cultural_caveats: None specific. This is Mint's home emotion in Slowly Growing - keep it subtle and consistent.
rig_hint: R.pose 'chest' both hands (needs a 'wring' pose); R.breathe faster
ai_prompt_phrase: anxious, wringing hands, shoulders tense, shifting weight from foot to foot

evidence.note: Dael: anxiety split between the despair cluster and the panic-fear cluster (backward lean, upward gaze, lateral trunk lean); self-touch fidgeting is craft.

label_th: ประหลาดใจ สะดุ้ง

body_cues.head: jerks up/back
body_cues.arms: fly up/out briefly
body_cues.tempo_quality: very fast onset, then a hold (freeze)

silhouette_check: Stretched vertical shape; reads best as a change from the previous pose (needs motion or a before/after pair).

readability.disambiguate_with: After the hold, the next pose tells valence: lean in + smile = pleasant surprise; retreat = fear.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: startled, jumping slightly with arms flung open, body stiff

evidence.note: De Meijer (via Kleinsmith): surprise = straight trunk and legs, backward stepping, fast movement; Coulson: happiness and surprise confused.

label_th: รังเกียจ ขยะแขยง

body_cues.head: pulled back and turned away, slightly forward-down
body_cues.arms: crossed, or one hand pushing away
body_cues.hands: palm out toward the object, or covering nose/mouth

silhouette_check: Reads only with the object in frame.

readability.disambiguate_with: Object + covering the nose/mouth + turn-away; Coulson found disgust postures often unreadable alone.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: recoiling from the smell, turning away, hand covering nose

evidence.note: Coulson: many disgust postures 0% agreement; Wallbott (via Kleinsmith): crossed arms + head forward for disgust vs head back for pride; Dittrich included disgust in dance.

label_th: อ่อนโยน รักใคร่

body_cues.head: tilted toward the other
body_cues.arms: open or curved around the other
body_cues.hands: soft, may rest on the other's shoulder/back

silhouette_check: Rounded shapes and an inward lean; two characters' silhouettes should touch or nearly touch.

readability.disambiguate_with: Mutual lean and soft tempo; no tension in the hands.

cultural_caveats: Touch shoulder/arm/back, not the head. Never touch or pat another character's head, even a child's (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: leaning gently toward each other, heads tilted, soft rounded posture

evidence.note: Rounded postures read as warm (Aronoff via Kleinsmith); the rest is craft.

label_th: เหงา

body_cues.head: slightly down or looking out
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: toward a window, a phone, other people far away
body_cues.arms: wrapped around self or knees
body_cues.distance: large distance from others; small in frame

silhouette_check: Small figure + lots of negative space carries most of it (staging, not pose).

readability.disambiguate_with: The direction of the head (toward others or the outside) separates longing from plain sadness.

cultural_caveats: Seated hugging knees: Seated or lying: keep the soles pointed away from other characters, elders and any Buddha image (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: sitting alone hugging knees, looking out the window, small in a large empty room

evidence.note: Distance as relationship dial from proxemics (Sorokowska2017); the rest is staging craft.

label_th: เหนื่อย หมดแรง

body_cues.head: heavy, nodding
body_cues.arms: dangling, or propping the head
body_cues.tempo_quality: slow with occasional 'catch' (nodding off and jerking awake)

silhouette_check: Leaning on a wall/table plus a dropped head; props help.

readability.disambiguate_with: Yawn, eye-rub, or nodding-off loop; sadness has no physical-fatigue actions.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: walk step .65-.7 s, bob 5 px; R.pose 'chin'
ai_prompt_phrase: exhausted, shuffling with slumped shoulders, rubbing eyes, dragging feet

evidence.note: Slow gait carries low energy (Roether: speed is a key gait feature); fatigue actions are craft.

label_th: เบื่อ

body_cues.head: propped on one hand, tilting
body_cues.arms: one propping the head, one idle

silhouette_check: Head on hand at a table reads clearly.

readability.disambiguate_with: Aimless repetitive actions (spinning a pen) and a wandering head orientation.

cultural_caveats: Seated with legs stretched: Seated or lying: keep the soles pointed away from other characters, elders and any Buddha image (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: bored, chin propped on hand, slumped, idly spinning a pen

evidence.note: Not covered by the research read this session.

label_th: ความหวัง ตั้งตารอ

body_cues.head: lifted
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: toward the expected thing (door, results, sky)
body_cues.arms: close to the chest
body_cues.tempo_quality: contained energy: still with small rises

silhouette_check: Clasped hands at chest + lifted head read in MS.

readability.disambiguate_with: Hope looks UP and toward the thing; a wai is directed at a person with a head bow. Do not let 'hope hands' look like a wai to a Thai viewer unless intended.

cultural_caveats: Clasped hands at the chest can be read by Thai viewers as a wai or a prayer - choose fingers interlaced (hope) vs palms flat together (wai/prayer) on purpose.
ai_prompt_phrase: hands clasped at chest, rising on tiptoes, looking hopefully at the door

evidence.note: Rising/up components linked to happiness (Melzer); rest craft.

label_th: มุ่งมั่น

body_cues.head: level, chin slightly down
body_cues.arms: bent, ready; may roll up sleeves
body_cues.tempo_quality: steady, direct, strong but not sudden

silhouette_check: Squared front view with a slight forward lean; clear but can look like anger.

readability.disambiguate_with: Directed at a task or goal, not at a person; steady not jerky tempo; no approach toward another character.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: determined, rolling up sleeves, squared shoulders, striding toward the goal

evidence.note: Strong + direct components (Melzer anger set) minus 'sudden' and minus the person-target: craft derivation.

label_th: สงบ

body_cues.head: level, balanced
body_cues.arms: resting symmetrically

silhouette_check: Symmetry and verticality; risk of looking 'frozen' - add breathing.

readability.disambiguate_with: Upright and balanced (boredom slumps); slow visible breath.

cultural_caveats: Meditation-like seated posture: keep it respectful, do not pair with jokes about Buddhist practice (cultural sensitivity, craft).
ai_prompt_phrase: sitting upright and still, shoulders relaxed, breathing slowly, peaceful

evidence.note: Not directly studied in sources read; derived from low-arousal / balance conventions.

label_th: คิด ไตร่ตรอง

body_cues.head: tilted, slightly up
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: up and to the side, away from everyone
body_cues.arms: one arm across the body supporting the other

silhouette_check: Hand-to-chin is the most readable thinking shape.

readability.disambiguate_with: Head orientation up/away with a hold; then a change (idea) resolves it.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: R.emote(P,t,'think') (pupils up + chin pose + head tilt)
ai_prompt_phrase: thinking, hand on chin, head tilted, looking up to the side

evidence.note: Convention; Lasseter: the thought process must be visible before the action.

label_th: งง สับสน

body_cues.head: tilted strongly, may tilt the other way
body_cues.arms: small shrug, palms up
body_cues.hands: scratching own head, or palms up

silhouette_check: Head tilt + scratch reads; a shrug reads well in front view.

readability.disambiguate_with: Look back and forth between two objects; a question-mark shrug.

cultural_caveats: Scratching own head fine. Never touch or pat another character's head, even a child's (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: confused, scratching head, head tilted, looking from one thing to the other

evidence.note: Convention.

label_th: นึกออก

body_cues.head: snaps up
body_cues.head_orientation_gaze: up then straight at the partner/object
body_cues.arms: one hand flies up
body_cues.hands: index finger up, or a snap

silhouette_check: Finger up reads clearly in front or 3/4.

readability.disambiguate_with: Preceded by a thinking hold; the finger points UP (idea), not at someone.

cultural_caveats: Raising a finger at a senior to interrupt may read as rude in hierarchy-sensitive scenes (craft judgement, unverified).
ai_prompt_phrase: eyes widening with an idea, finger raised, body straightening

evidence.note: Anticipation (hold) then action - Disney principle.

label_th: จดจ่อ

body_cues.head: forward, toward the task
body_cues.arms: close in, working

silhouette_check: Hunch toward a task looks like defeat in silhouette unless the task is visible.

confusable_with: defeat (Kleinsmith: both had shoulders slumped forward, arms down/diagonal)
readability.disambiguate_with: Show the task and the head orientation toward it; hands active, not limp.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: leaning in, absorbed, working carefully on a small object

evidence.note: Kleinsmith (Wii): concentrating vs defeated share slumped shoulders and arms down - disambiguate with task/hands.

label_th: ยอมแพ้ หมดหวัง

body_cues.head: dropped
body_cues.arms: hanging down and diagonally across the body

silhouette_check: Collapsed forward shape; needs context (lost game, rejected paper).

readability.disambiguate_with: Something drops (object, shoulders, body to a seat) at the moment of giving up; then stillness.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
ai_prompt_phrase: shoulders slumping forward, arms hanging, letting the paper fall, sinking onto a bench

evidence.note: Kleinsmith (Wii defeated) + Tracy (losing: slumped shoulders, narrowed chest).

label_th: ตั้งใจฟัง
intent: show the speaker they are heard

body_cues.head: small nods, slight tilt
body_cues.spine_torso: oriented toward the speaker, slight lean in
body_cues.arms: still, open
body_cues.tempo_quality: mostly still, nods on the speaker's key words

silhouette_check: Body and head turned toward the speaker is visible even for faceless characters.

readability.disambiguate_with: Keep the listener's head/body pointed at the speaker; nod on stressed words.

cultural_caveats: Listening to an elder: slightly lowered head and stillness are polite (craft, consistent with ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: listening attentively, turned toward the friend, nodding gently

evidence.note: Orientation as attention cue (Langton); amusement/engagement head toward interlocutor (Dael); nods are craft.

label_th: เมิน ไม่สนใจ

body_cues.head: turned away
body_cues.shoulders: turned, one shoulder toward the other
body_cues.arms: crossed or busy with something else

silhouette_check: Back or shoulder to the other character reads immediately.

readability.disambiguate_with: Ignoring is upright and busy; shame is collapsed.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: R.turn away; R.look away with body
ai_prompt_phrase: turning her back on him, arms crossed, looking at her phone

evidence.note: Head and body orientation signal the direction of attention (Langton; Emery).

label_th: หันไปมอง

body_cues.head: turns toward the target
body_cues.arms: may point
body_cues.hands: pointing or open hand toward the target

silhouette_check: Head turn must be large enough to read without eyes - exaggerate the angle.

readability.disambiguate_with: Add pointing or a body turn for a stronger cue; viewers' attention follows automatically.

cultural_caveats: Point with the hand, never the foot (ThailandFoundation2024).
ai_prompt_phrase: turning head and body to look at the product on the table, hand gesturing toward it

evidence.note: Gaze, head orientation and pointing all cue attention and trigger reflexive orienting (Langton).

body_cues.head: toward the target
body_cues.arms: one arm extended
body_cues.tempo_quality: preparation -> stroke on the stressed word -> brief hold -> retraction

silhouette_check: Extended arm away from the body reads in silhouette.

readability.disambiguate_with: Point at things/places; pointing at a person's face reads as accusation.

cultural_caveats: Never point with the foot. Pointing a finger at an elder or at a Buddha image is impolite in Thailand; an open hand is the safer default (general etiquette guidance; finger-pointing detail unverified).
ai_prompt_phrase: pointing with an open hand toward the shop sign

evidence.note: Deictic gesture type (McNeill via ShattuckHufnagelRen); stroke aligns with pitch accent.

label_th: อธิบายด้วยมือ
intent: show size, shape or action while talking

body_cues.head: toward the listener between gestures
body_cues.arms: hands in front of the torso drawing the shape
body_cues.tempo_quality: stroke on the stressed syllable; one gesture per idea

silhouette_check: Gesture space in front of the body, not hidden behind it.

readability.disambiguate_with: Gesture should ADD information not in the words (size, direction, action).

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: R.pose 'open'/'reach' timed to TTS stress; R.arm custom
ai_prompt_phrase: explaining with hands, showing how big the fish was

evidence.note: Hostetter meta-analysis: gestures help comprehension, more for motor actions and when not redundant; strokes align with pitch accents.

label_th: เน้นคำ

body_cues.head: small nod on the stress
body_cues.arms: small down-flick
body_cues.tempo_quality: brief flick on the stressed syllable, then rest

silhouette_check: Small - only visible in MS/MCU.

readability.disambiguate_with: Use once or twice per line maximum; constant beats look nervous.

cultural_caveats: Thai is tonal; aligning beats to Thai prominence is untested (gap).
rig_hint: R.nod 1 + small arm flick on stressed syllable
ai_prompt_phrase: talking with a small emphatic hand flick on the key word

evidence.note: McNeill beats; strokes of non-referential gestures align with pitch-accented syllables (English).

label_th: ชั่งใจ

body_cues.head: tilts side to side
body_cues.arms: both forearms out, palms up
body_cues.hands: palms up, moving up/down like scales

silhouette_check: Two palms up at waist height read in front view.

readability.disambiguate_with: Hands as scale pans while saying 'this ... or that'.

cultural_caveats: None specific.
rig_hint: R.pose 'shrug' variant with alternating arm heights
ai_prompt_phrase: weighing two options, palms up, tilting head side to side

label_th: ไหว้ทั่วไป

readability.disambiguate_with: Palms flat together + head bow toward a person = wai.
